title: We worship without temples or statues
source_text: Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἡγοῦμαι ὅτι τούτους μόνους ἠπίστατο ὁ Κέλσος. καὶ ἵνα δοκῇ ἑκὼν παραλιπεῖν τὰ παραπλήσια, εἶπε τό· καὶ ἄλλους ἔχοι τις ἂν εἰπεῖν τοιούσδε πλείονας. ἔστω δ᾿ οὖν καὶ δεδόσθω τοιούσδε γεγονέναι πλείονας, μηδὲν ὠφεληκότας τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος. τί τούτων ἕκαστον εὑρεθείη ἂν πρὸς τὸ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἔργον καὶ τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ παράδοξα, περὶ ὧν ἐπὶ πλεῖον εἰρήκαμεν; μετὰ ταῦτα παραπλήσιον ἡμᾶς οἴεται πεποιηκέναι τὸν, ὥς φησιν ὁ Κέλσος, ἁλόντα καὶ ἀποθανόντα θρησκεύοντας τοῖς Γέταις σέβουσι τὸν Ζάμολξιν καὶ Κίλιξι τὸν Μόψον καὶ Ἀκαρνᾶσι τὸν Ἀμφίλοχον καὶ Θηβαίοις τὸν Ἀμφιάρεω καὶ Λεβαδίοις τὸν Τροφώνιον. καὶ ἐν τούτοις δὲ ἐλέγξομεν αὐτὸν οὐκ εὐλόγως ἡμᾶς ὁμοιώσαντα τοῖς προειρημένοις. οἱ μὲν γὰρ νεὼς καὶ ἀγάλματα κατεσκεύασαν τοῖς κατειλεγμένοις, ἡμεῖς δὲ τὴν διὰ τῶν τοιούτων τιμὴν ἀνελόντες ἀπὸ τοῦ θείου (ὡς ἁρμοζόντων μᾶλλον δαιμονίοις οὐκ οἶδ᾿ ὅπως ἱδρυμένοις ἔν τινι τόπῳ, ὃν ἤτοι προκαταλαμβάνουσιν ἢ διά τινων τελετῶν ἀχθέντες καὶ μαγγανειῶν ὥσπερ οἰκοῦσιν) τεθήπαμεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν τὸν νοῦν ἡμῶν μεταθέντα ἀπὸ παντὸς αἰσθητοῦ. ὡς οὐ μόνον φθαρτοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ φθαρησομένου, καὶ ἀνάγοντα ἐπὶ τὴν μετὰ ὀρθοῦ βίου πρὸς τὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεὸν τιμὴν μετ᾿ εὐχῶν, ἃς προσάγομεν αὐτῷ ὡς διὰ μεταξὺ ὄντος τῆς τοῦ ἀγενήτου καὶ τῆς τῶν γενητῶν πάντων φύσεως, καὶ φέροντος μὲν ἡμῖν τὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς εὐεργεσίας διακομίζοντος δ᾿ ἡμῶν τρόπον ἀρχιερέως τὰς εὐχὰς πρὸς τὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεόν.
pass_a_gloss: I then think that these alone Celsus knew (ἐπίσταμαι); and that he may seem (δοκέω) willingly (ἑκών) to have left out (παραλείπω) the similar (παραπλήσια), he said: and others one could say of such sort, more (πλείονας). Well, let it be (ἔστω) and let it be granted (δίδωμι) many such to have existed, having benefited (ὠφελέω) the race of men in nothing. What would each of these be found [to be] against (πρός) the work (ἔργον) of Jesus and the marvels (παράδοξα) about him, about which we have spoken at length (ἐπὶ πλεῖον)? After these he thinks us to have done (ποιέω) something similar, worshipping (θρησκεύω) him who, as Celsus says, was captured (ἁλίσκομαι) and died (ἀποθνῄσκω), to the Getae revering (σέβω) Zamolxis and Cilicians Mopsus and Acarnanians Amphilochus and Thebans Amphiaraus and Lebadeans Trophonius. And in these too we shall refute (ἐλέγχω) him as not reasonably (εὐλόγως) having likened (ὁμοιόω) us to those aforesaid. For they built (κατασκευάζω) temples (νεῴ) and images/statues (ἀγάλματα) to those listed (καταλέγω), but we, having taken away (ἀναιρέω) the honour (τιμή) through such things from the divine (τὸ θεῖον) (as fitting rather demons (δαιμόνια) established (ἱδρύω) I know not how in some place, which they either occupy beforehand (προκαταλαμβάνω) or, led (ἄγω) by certain rites (τελεταί) and sorceries (μαγγανεῖαι), as it were dwell in (οἰκέω)), are amazed at Jesus who transferred (μετατίθημι) our mind (νοῦς) from everything perceptible (αἰσθητόν) as not only corruptible (φθαρτόν) but also going to be corrupted (φθαρησόμενον), and who leads up (ἀνάγω) to the honour, with upright life (ὀρθὸς βίος), toward the God over all with prayers (εὐχαί), which we bring (προσάγω) to him as through [one] being between (μεταξύ) the nature (φύσις) of the uncreated/unoriginate (ἀγένητος) and the nature of all created things (γενητά), and bearing (φέρω) to us the benefits (εὐεργεσίαι) from the Father, and conveying (διακομίζω) in the manner (τρόπον) of a high priest (ἀρχιερεύς) our prayers to the God over all.
pass_b_english: For my part, I think that these were the only ones Celsus knew. And so that he may seem to have passed over similar cases by choice, he said, “And one could name many others of this kind.” Well, let it be so, and let it be granted that there have been many such men, who did nothing at all to help the human race. What would each of them be found to be when set beside the work of Jesus and the wonders told of him, of which we have spoken at length?

After this he supposes that we, in worshipping one who, as Celsus says, “was captured and died,” have done something like the Getae, who revere Zamolxis, the Cilicians, who revere Mopsus, the Acarnanians Amphilochus, the Thebans Amphiaraus, and the people of Lebadea Trophonius. Here too we shall prove that he had no good reason to liken us to those just named. For they built temples and statues to those whom he lists; but we have taken away from the Divine the honour paid by such means, as more fitting for demons, which are somehow settled in a particular place, a place they either seize beforehand or, drawn there by certain rites and sorceries, in a manner inhabit. We, rather, look with wonder on Jesus, who has turned our mind away from everything that the senses perceive, as being not only perishable but also bound to perish, and who leads it up to honour the God over all with an upright life and with prayers. These we offer to him through one who stands, as it were, between the nature of the uncreated and the nature of all created things, who brings us the benefits that come from the Father and, in the manner of a high priest, carries our prayers to the God over all.

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 34 (Koetschau 3.34). Celsus’s phrase ‘καὶ ἄλλους ἔχοι τις ἂν εἰπεῖν τοιούσδε πλείονας’ is introduced by ‘εἶπε τό’ and set in quotation marks as his words; ‘ἁλόντα καὶ ἀποθανόντα’ is marked by Origen as Celsus’s (‘ὥς φησιν ὁ Κέλσος’) and is quoted. The list of peoples and their worship (Getae and Zamolxis, Cilicians and Mopsus, Acarnanians and Amphilochus, Thebans and Amphiaraus, Lebadeans and Trophonius) is reported by Origen and is left unquoted. ‘ἐκ τοῦ θείου’ / ‘ἀπὸ τοῦ θείου’: ‘τὸ θεῖον’ rendered ‘the Divine’ (meaning God), capitalised. The parenthesis (ὡς ἁρμοζόντων … ὥσπερ οἰκοῦσιν) is kept as a subordinate explanation rather than in brackets; the main verb ‘τεθήπαμεν’ (we look with wonder on) follows it, and the sentence is split at that point (‘We, rather, look with wonder on Jesus’) for readability; ‘rather’ renders the contrast of ‘ἡμεῖς δέ’ with ‘οἱ μέν’. ‘ὡς διὰ μεταξὺ ὄντος τῆς τοῦ ἀγενήτου καὶ τῆς τῶν γενητῶν πάντων φύσεως’: the staged text spells ἀγένητος/γενητά with one nu, so ‘uncreated’/‘created’ (not ‘unbegotten’/‘begotten’); Origen’s spelling in other witnesses varies, and this is noted as a point to check against the raw edition. ‘αὐτῷ’ in ‘ἃς προσάγομεν αὐτῷ’ refers to the God over all; the English ‘to him’ follows the Greek. Possible allusions, not cited inline: ‘between’ the uncreated and the created may echo 1 Timothy 2:5 (one mediator between God and men); Jesus as high priest carrying prayers echoes the Letter to the Hebrews generally (for example Hebrews 4:14–16; 7:25), but no single verse is quoted.

‘be found to be beside’ made ‘be found to be when set beside’ (πρός, comparison)
Confirmed Celsus’s two quoted phrases and the unquoted list of cults; ‘to him’ (αὐτῷ) left as in the Greek, nearest antecedent the God over all
No inline Scripture: mediator and high-priest language left as uncertain echoes in the note
